matchstick.title: Prefer intra-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: When trying to fix the equation, first attempt to move a single matchstick within the same character; this often yields a valid transformation without breaking other symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation is invalid and you need to move exactly one matchstick.
matchstick.example: Attempting an inter-character move before checking possible intra-character changes.

matchstick.title: Validate symbols after stick move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, verify that each resulting character corresponds to a valid Roman numeral or operator; an invalid shape indicates an illegal move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after any stick relocation, before evaluating arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Creating a single diagonal stick that does not form any Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Avoid single angled sticks
matchstick.principle: A solitary diagonal stick does not represent any Roman numeral; ensure that removing a diagonal from X or V does not leave a lone diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When moving a diagonal stick from a V or X character.
matchstick.example: Turning X into a single diagonal stick, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Consider inter-character stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If no intra-character move yields a valid equation, explore moving a stick from one character to another, ensuring both source and destination remain valid symbols.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After exhausting intra-character possibilities without success.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from an I to a V, leaving the I empty.

matchstick.title: Verify arithmetic after stick move
matchstick.principle: Compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation after any transformation; the equality must hold.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming that all symbols are valid.
matchstick.example: Accepting a transformation that yields a syntactically correct equation but with unequal values.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign after stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If a stick is taken from the '=' sign, ensure the remaining symbol still forms a valid equality sign (i.e., retains two horizontal sticks).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moves that involve the '=' character.
matchstick.example: Removing one horizontal stick from '=', turning it into a '-' sign.

matchstick.title: Validate whole numeral strings for proper Roman numeral syntax
matchstick.principle: After any stick move, verify that each multi-character numeral follows standard Roman numeral order and subtraction rules.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After confirming individual symbols are valid, before arithmetic.
matchstick.example: Creating 'IIX' which violates Roman numeral syntax.

matchstick.title: Intra-character diagonal transformation (V↔X)
matchstick.principle: When a character is V or X (both composed of two diagonal sticks), moving one diagonal within the same character can change V to X or X to V, adjusting its value by ±5.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a value change of ±5 may resolve the equation.
matchstick.example: Changing X to V, decreasing the value by 5, without affecting other symbols.

matchstick.title: Transform '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick to an adjacent I
matchstick.principle: If a '+' operator and an adjacent 'I' numeral are present, moving the vertical stick from '+' to the I can turn '+' into '-' and increase the I to V, potentially fixing the equation.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' next to an I and a value adjustment is needed.
matchstick.example: Turning '+ I' into '- V' by moving the vertical stick.

matchstick.title: Intra-character operator transformation (e.g., '+' → '=', '-' → '=') by rotating a stick within the same operator
matchstick.principle: Operators can be changed by rotating a stick within the same character; for example, turning '+' into '=' by rotating its vertical stick to horizontal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When changing the operator type may balance the equation without moving sticks between characters.
matchstick.example: Rotating the vertical stick of '+' to make it '=', creating a double horizontal operator.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character transformations (e.g., X→V) before inter‑character moves
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model often jumps to moving sticks between characters, missing simpler intra‑character changes that could solve the puzzle.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: First enumerate possible intra‑character moves (e.g., V↔X, I↔V) before considering inter‑character relocations.

matchstick.description: Leaving a single angled stick after moving a diagonal from X or V (invalid numeral)
matchstick.why_it_happens: Removing a diagonal from X or V leaves a lone diagonal, which does not correspond to any Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that any diagonal removal is paired with a transformation that keeps both source and destination characters valid, e.g., converting V to X instead of removing a diagonal outright.

matchstick.description: Not evaluating the arithmetic result after each candidate transformation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may accept a syntactically correct equation without checking if the numeric values actually match.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute the numeric values of both sides after any move and verify equality before finalizing the answer.

matchstick.description: Overlooking intra‑character operator transformations (e.g., '+' → '=', '-' → '=') and assuming operator changes require moving sticks between characters
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes operator changes need inter‑character stick moves, missing the possibility of rotating a stick within the operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Consider rotating sticks within operators as a valid single‑stick move before attempting inter‑character relocations.

matchstick.description: Omitting the equality sign in the final answer
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes drops the '=' when constructing the output, leading to an invalid equation format.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure the final answer line contains a complete equation with a single '=' sign separating the left and right sides.
